prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles, built on pH-dependent lipid physical chemistry and rapid-mixing self-assembly, that deliver nucleic-acid medicines into cells

statement.case_for: I am changing my preferred configuration from B062 (Gray and Winkler) to B045 with Cullis, Hope and Madden. The round-1 exchange tested B062 and it did not hold up as a lead. Aqvist, Linke and Zou each asked what the citation would say that the 1992 Marcus prize does not, and I could not give an answer that persuades me over the credit gaps around Beratan, Onuchic and Dutton. B045 is what I look for in biophysical chemistry: a mechanism stated in physical terms. The ionizable headgroup has a pKa tuned so that the particle is nearly neutral in blood and becomes charged in the acidifying endosome. That charge change drives lipid polymorphism and membrane destabilization, and rapid mixing sets the self-assembly kinetics that make particles of defined size. The consequences are demonstrated and not promised: an approved siRNA therapy and billions of mRNA vaccine doses, reproduced by many independent groups. Sparr's argument that the decisive step is the Vancouver ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing line, and not the broader delivery-materials concept, gives a three-name cut that I can defend by mechanism. It is the only candidate on the shortlist that combines a clear physical mechanism, full maturity and a credit chain that can fit within three names, once the expert reports confirm who developed the ionizable lipid and the formulation process.
statement.case_against: The credit is the weak point. Langer and Anderson (lipidoid and combinatorial discovery) and MacLachlan (first clinical siRNA formulations) are excluded by this cut, and Aili is entitled to say that the broader delivery concept is part of the achievement. Part of the formulation chemistry is industrial and partly proprietary, which makes priority harder to document than in an academic literature. The 2023 Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification for mRNA, and the citation must make clear that this prize is for the vehicle and its chemistry and not for the vaccine. I am also drawn to the physical-mechanism framing of the pKa and endosome story, which is a bias to disclose. If the expert reports show the decisive step lies with Langer's lipidoid line, the configuration changes.

responses.point: Sparr argues that the enabling chemistry is pH-dependent ionizable lipids, lipid polymorphism and rapid-mixing self-assembly, tracing to Cullis, Hope and Madden, and that pairing Cullis with Langer would credit a broader delivery concept than the lipid physical chemistry.
responses.response: I now adopt your trio. You know lipid self-assembly better than I do, and the pKa-controlled charge switch plus the polymorphic transition in the endosome is the sort of quantifiable mechanism I want a citation to rest on. I would ask you to confirm that the ionizable-lipid step and the rapid-mixing process were in fact established in the Vancouver work and not taken over from industrial partners, because that is what the expert reports must settle. If it holds, we agree on both the names and the framing, and I think your point answers the question the chair raised about who holds the decisive step.

responses.point: Aili prefers Cullis and Langer, treating Langer as the representative of the broader delivery-materials concept and combinatorial lipid discovery that made the platform general.
responses.response: I agree with you on maturity and impact, which I called beyond dispute in round 1, and I have moved to B045 for that reason. I do not follow you on Langer. Lipidoid and polymer delivery is a different design strategy from pH-tuned lipid physical chemistry, and its role in the clinical siRNA and mRNA products is less direct. The citation I propose is deliberately narrow so that it is accurate. It leaves out Langer, Anderson and MacLachlan, and I accept that this has a cost. If you can show that the lipidoid line supplied the ionizable lipids in the approved products, that would change my view, and I would like to know which of the two paths the products actually followed.

responses.point: Aqvist asks whether Gray and Winkler's protein tunneling is a distinct achievement or an experimental completion of the 1992 Marcus prize, noting that Beratan, Onuchic and Dutton also contributed.
responses.response: Your question is fair, and I cannot answer it well enough. The distance dependence of tunneling through protein is a result in its own right, but the citation would say little that Marcus did not already say, and the pathway theorists and Dutton mean any two-name credit is incomplete. I therefore withdraw B062 as my lead and keep it as a first alternative. I am not asking others to follow me there. On your own B029, I still need an answer on which results depend on the fictitious-dynamics formulation and not on Born-Oppenheimer MD, since without that I cannot place it ahead of a mature, mechanistically clear entry such as B045.

responses.point: Zou moved to B016 with Miyasaka, Park and Snaith, argued that the prize concerns the discovery and not product deployment, and called B062 the more incremental of the two options.
responses.response: I accept the incremental point on B062. On B016 you are right that we need not wait for modules to last 25 years, and I called the scientific impact undisputed in round 1. My reservation, which you concede in part, is that the mechanism of why these cells work, ion migration, phase segregation and the role of defects, is still contested, and that Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis have credible claims that make any trio look arbitrary. For me that is a question of settled mechanism and credit. It is not a question of whether the product is on the market. I list B016 as a second alternative and could support it if the expert reports settle priority and the mechanism becomes clearer.

responses.point: Linke argues that the perovskite discovery is the absorber and its photophysics, which are established, and that whether modules last 25 years is an engineering question. He also asks what a B062 citation would say that Marcus did not.
responses.response: I take your answer on B062 and agree that it was a hard question to answer. On perovskites, I accept that I ranked B016 eighth mainly because it is outside my field, and the photophysics case is stronger than my opening ranking suggested. I still weigh the unresolved attribution between six names more heavily than you do, and I think a prize that can be defended name by name is better than one which depends on a priority chain I cannot yet verify. If the committee does find B016 more compelling in the end, I would not oppose the Miyasaka, Park and Snaith trio.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports confirm that the ionizable lipid and the rapid-mixing process originate with Cullis, Hope and Madden, or whether Langer, Anderson or MacLachlan hold a decisive step that a three-name cut should include.
How the citation should be worded to separate the delivery vehicle from the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification.
Whether any single configuration can gather five of eight votes, since B045, B016 and B029 each have a different group of supporters and each faces a different attribution or maturity objection.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional connection to Cullis, Hope, Madden or any other shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. My earlier note on B062 being close to my research on electron and proton transfer is now moot for my preferred part, though it remains as a disclosure if B062 returns as an alternative. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which bears on none of the candidates in my configuration, and no recusal is sought. I also disclose a bias toward candidates described through a physical mechanism, which I applied to B045.
